headline: Wolves favourites but Peixoto under pressure against Watford
summary: Watford arrive at Molineux on Saturday after a 5-1 defeat at Cardiff, having lost four of their last five and sitting 20th. Wolves are seventh, but Tuesday's 1-1 home draw with Portsmouth left Cesar Peixoto reportedly fighting for his future, according to Football Insider. Adam Armstrong has missed two games with a back injury, and Raul Jimenez is out until the new year. Even so, the market makes Wolves 68.5% favourites: Watford have conceded 2.0 expected goals a game. The handicap line is Wolves minus 1.25, so the market expects a win by about one clear goal.
read: Wolves are clear 68.5% favourites at Molineux, rated about 1.3 goals better than a Watford side that has lost four of five and conceded 12 in the process. The backdrop is pressure: Wolves have gone three home games without a win and their manager is reported to be fighting for his job, while up front they are missing Armstrong and Jimenez, with a teenage striker starting.

facts.fact: Wolves are 68.5% favourites to win at home, with Watford at 12.4% and the draw at 19.1%.
facts.meaning: The market makes Wolves more than five times as likely to win as Watford — a heavy home favourite, not a close game.

facts.fact: Football Insider reports that sources say Cesar Peixoto is fighting for his future at Wolves and could be sacked if they fail to beat Watford.
Watford's last five Championship results read WLLLL, with 12 goals conceded in that run.
facts.meaning: A side arriving in poor defensive form is exactly the profile the market is pricing as a heavy underdog.

facts.fact: Adam Armstrong has missed Wolves' last two matches with a back injury, and Raul Jimenez is out until at least the new year following surgery.
facts.meaning: Wolves are without their two most established forwards, which is why a teenager has been leading the line.

facts.fact: Wolves were held 1-1 at home by Portsmouth on Tuesday, needing a response after back-to-back defeats.
facts.meaning: Three games without a win at Molineux is the backdrop to the pressure on the manager and to the game's tension.

facts.fact: Watford ended their poor run by beating Charlton 2-0 at Vicarage Road, with Luca Kjerrumgaard and Jordan Zemura scoring.
facts.meaning: They arrive off a win rather than a defeat, and the coach called the mood good afterwards — not a team in freefall.

facts.fact: Watford have conceded an average of 2.0 expected goals across their last five matches, including 3.67 in the 1-5 defeat at Cardiff.
facts.meaning: They are not just conceding goals, they are conceding clear chances — the most direct explanation for a handicap this size.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line is -1.34 in Wolves' favour, with the main line at -1.25.
facts.meaning: The market sees Wolves as roughly 1.3 goals the better team — a comfortable win is the expectation, not just a win.

sources.fact: Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto is hopeful that Adam Armstrong and Kieran Trippier will be fit to face Watford on Saturday.
Wolves left Adam Armstrong and Kieran Trippier out of the 1-1 draw with Portsmouth and will check on both before the Watford match.
Adam Armstrong has missed Wolves' last two matches with a back injury, and Raul Jimenez is out until at least the new year following surgery.
Football Insider reports that sources say Cesar Peixoto is fighting for his future at Wolves and could be sacked if they fail to beat Watford this weekend.
Wolves' promotion bid suffered a setback as Portsmouth snatched a 1-1 draw at Molineux on Tuesday.
Wolves came from behind to win 2-1 at Burnley, extending Burnley's home league winless run to a full year.

Watford head coach Alessio Dionisi said he was "very happy" after the 2-0 win over Charlton, adding "we stay together and work together."
